newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB boosts Australia wheat pool prices by A$10/t.
newsitem.headline: AWB boosts Australia wheat pool prices by A$10/t.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it raised estimated pool prices for all grades in the Number Two pool by A$10.00 a tonne.
The price of benchmark grade Australian Standard White (ASW) rises to A$195.00 a tonne.

AWB general manager merchandising Ron Storey said the pool price rises were due to recent improvements in world prices and to continued concern about the level of Australian production, particularly on the country's east coast.
The AWB has also increased its estimate of pool prices for 1997/98 wheat. The ASW price has been increased to A$195.00 a tonne from the previous estimate of A$180.00-A$190.00 a tonne.
AWB also announced a reduced estimate of the 1997/98 wheat crop at 14 to 15 million tonnes, down by one million tonnes.
1996/97 No.2 Pool and 1997/98 pool prices at August 4
Note: 1996/97 No 1 pool closed. Next revision August 18.
